title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page states the conclusion of a computation begun on the previous page (§52 of the continuation of La Longue Marche). Notation: S_0^+ = SL(2,Z), and S_0 is presumably GL(2,Z).

(114) Tower of normal subgroups of SL(2,Z):
- Π = Π[2] = Γ(2), the principal congruence subgroup of level 2, of index 6.
- Π_0, of index 2 in Γ(2), generated by the λ_i = -ℓ_i. Here ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ are the standard parabolic generators of Γ(2), e.g. ℓ_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]]. Π_0 is the torsion-free lift of Γ̄(2) that does not contain -1. It is free of rank 2: the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, inside the λ-line uniformisation.
- Π_00, of index 3 in Π_0, contains [Π_0,Π_0]. It is the normal subgroup generated by λ_1λ_0^{-1}. So Π_0/Π_00 ≅ Z/3 and λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞ all map to the same generator, consistent with λ_0λ_1λ_∞ = 1. Geometrically this is the cyclic Z/3 cover of P^1 minus 3 points, totally ramified over 0, 1 and ∞. That is the Fermat cubic x^3 + y^3 = 1, an elliptic curve with j = 0.

The aim is to show this whole tower is congruence, cut out at level 12. Two facts are used:
- (115) SL(2,Z)/Γ(12) ≅ SL(2,Z/12), and SL(2,Z/12) ≅ SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3) by the Chinese remainder theorem.
- (116) A tower of subgroups of H = SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3), of order 48·24, matching (114):
  - Π^• = sl(2,F_2) × SL(2,F_3), order 8·24, index 6.
  - Π_0^• = sl(2,F_2)' × SL(2,F_3), order 4·24, index 2.
  - Π_00^• = sl(2,F_2)' × Syl_2, order 4·8, index 3.

(117) explains the pieces:
- (a) Ker(SL(2,Z/4) → SL(2,Z/2)) = {1+2X : X ∈ M_2(F_2), tr X = 0} ≅ sl(2,F_2) as an additive group. The trace condition holds because det(1+2X) ≡ 1+2 tr X mod 4.
- (b) sl(2,F_2)' = {0, I+E, I+F, E+F} is the conjugation-stable complement of the scalars μ = {0, I}, which correspond to ±1. Its nonzero elements are exactly the reductions of λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞; for example -ℓ_0 ≡ 1 + 2(I+E) mod 4.
- (c) Syl_2 = Ker(SL(2,F_3) → PSL(2,F_3) = A_4 → Z/3) is the normal Sylow 2-subgroup of order 8.

The argument is completed on the next page. The map SL(2,Z) → H sends the groups of (114) into those of (116). Both towers have the same indices (6, 12, 36), so each group in (114) is the full inverse image of its counterpart. In particular Π_00 is a congruence subgroup of level dividing 12 and index 36 in SL(2,Z).

The left margin NB seems to say that the quotient SL(2,Z)/Π_00 ≅ H/Π_00^• is identified with (SL(2,Z/4)/sl(2,F_2)') × (SL(2,F_3)/Syl_2), an extension of S_3 by μ. It is then compared with S_0^+/Π_0.

This serves the Longue Marche programme: describing explicit finite quotients of SL(2,Z) and of the 'Teichmüller' groups, and deciding which natural normal subgroups are congruence. The next page compares the result with the quotient SL(2,Z)/[Π_0,Π_0] and with the subgroup M_0 of (99)/(108).
errors: Syl_2 of SL(2,F_3) is written '≃ D_4'; after a crossed-out attempt the image clearly reads D_4. This is wrong: the Sylow 2-subgroup of SL(2,F_3) is the quaternion group Q_8, since -1 is its unique involution. The error does not affect the order count (8) or the index argument.
Minor: the transcription's first line says the subgroup has 'indice 3 dans Π_0' while naming Π_0. It must refer to Π_00 ⊂ SL(2,Z).
Minor: sl(2,F_2)' is a conjugation-invariant additive complement of μ, but it is not a Lie subalgebra, since [I+E, I+F] = I. Grothendieck only calls μ a Lie subalgebra, so the text is accurate.

ideas.what: Tower Γ(2) ⊃ Π_0 (the torsion-free lift generated by -ℓ_i) ⊃ Π_00 (the Z/3 'diagonal' quotient, i.e. the Fermat cubic cover of the λ-line) inside SL(2,Z), with each group identified as the inverse image of an explicit subgroup of SL(2,Z/12) ≅ SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3)
ideas.modern_name: Congruence property of subgroups of Fermat-type in Γ(2); explicit level-12 description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard theory of congruence subgroups. On which Fermat groups are congruence: Rohrlich and Kenku (1970s–80s)

ideas.what: Kernel of SL(2,Z/4) → SL(2,Z/2) identified with the additive group sl(2,F_2), split S_3-equivariantly as the scalars μ plus an invariant Klein-four complement made of the images of λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Level-raising kernel ≅ adjoint module sl_2(F_p); characteristic-2 splitting of sl_2

ideas.what: Normal Sylow 2-subgroup of SL(2,F_3) as the kernel of SL(2,F_3) → Z/3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine verification that a specific normal subgroup of SL(2,Z) is congruence of level 12: the index-3 subgroup of the free lift of Γ̄(2), corresponding to the Fermat cubic Z/3 cover of P^1 minus 3 points. All ingredients are classical, and congruence questions for Fermat-type subgroups are treated in the literature. The only notable feature is a small error (D_4 instead of Q_8). Nothing here appears to be new.
transcription_corrections: Top line should read roughly: 'le sous-groupe invariant Π_00 ⊂ Sl(2,Z), d'indice 3 dans Π_0, qui est l'image inverse d'un sous-groupe ... de Sl(2,Z/12Z)'. The machine text wrongly writes Π_0 for the subgroup of index 3.
In (116), Syl_2 is followed by a crossed-out word and then '≃ D_4', which is clearly legible in the image. Mathematically it should be Q_8.
In (117c), the image reads 'Ker(Sl(2,Z/3Z) → S_3^+)', the cyclic group of order 3, followed by 'sous-groupe de Sylow, d'ordre 8 (qui est distingué)'.
The superscript marks on Π, Π_0, Π_00 in (116) are dots or primes. The next page calls them Π', Π_0', Π_00'.
In (114), the parenthetical after Π_00 reads '(⊃[Π_0,Π_0])', and 'sous-groupes invariants (ou dans S_0)' probably means invariant in S_0 = GL(2,Z).
